{{Short description|American statistician (1957–2018)}}
'''Joan Georgette Staniswalis''' (July 25, 1957 – April 13, 2018) was an American statistician. She made significant contributions to the theory and biomedical applications of statistics, including the effects of [[air quality]] and [[racial inequality]] on health.{{r|obit}}

==Education and career==
Staniswalis was born in [[Fort Lewis (Washington)|Fort Lewis, Washington]]. Her father was in the U.S. Army, and she lived in [[Panama City|Panama City, Panama]] during his periods of service.{{r|obit}}

She attended [[California State University, Fullerton]] beginning in 1975, and graduated in 1979 with high honors in mathematics and a minor in physics.{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. in 1985 at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. Her dissertation, ''Local Bandwidth Selection for Kernel Estimates'', was supervised by John A. Rice.{{r|cv|mg}}

In 1984, she became a lecturer in [[business statistics]] at [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] (VCU). In the following year, she shifted to the department of [[biostatistics]] in VCU's [[VCU School of Medicine|Medical College of Virginia]]. She moved in 1990 to the [[University of Texas at El Paso]] (UTEP), where she was promoted to full professor in 1999. She remained at UTEP for the rest of her career, with the exception of a term in 2001 as visiting professor and interim associate dean at [[New Mexico State University]].{{r|cv}} She retired to become a [[professor emeritus]] in 2016.{{r|obit}}

At UTEP, she directed the Statistical Consulting Laboratory from 1997 to 2003.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Staniswalis was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2001, "for important contributions to nonparametric regression and its application to biomedical research; for collaborative research accomplishments and administrative leadership in consulting; for mentoring of students and junior researchers".{{r|cv|obit}}
